description.text: The MAGUK family proteins are multifunctional scaffolding proteins that play pivotal roles in cell polarity, tight junction biogenesis, and synaptic transmembrane protein anchoring. They are involved in various cellular processes including the regulation of neutrophil polarity, epithelial cell polarity, vascular lumen formation, and neuronal progenitor cell survival. These proteins are essential for the correct localization and trafficking of various cellular components, such as adherens junction proteins, myelin proteins, and vesicular markers. They also participate in signal transduction pathways, potentially influencing mTOR signaling and NF-kappa-B activation. Additionally, they have a role in the maintenance and organization of cerebellar progenitor cells and retinal development. The MAGUK family members contain characteristic domains such as PDZ, L27, and PRBH, which mediate their interactions with other proteins and membranes.

description.text: This family consists of the p55 subfamily of membrane-associated guanylate kinases (MAGUKs), which includes the membrane protein, palmitoylated (MPP) proteins 1-7 (such as PALS1 and PALS2), as well as the peripheral plasma membrane protein CASK and its invertebrate homologs like LIN-2. MAGUKs are scaffolding proteins that play crucial roles in the assembly of multiprotein complexes at regions of cell-cell contact, such as epithelial tight junctions and neuronal synapses [[cite:PUB00075027], [cite:PUB00050845]]. Members of this family share a conserved core architecture consisting of a PDZ domain, an SH3 domain, and a catalytically inactive guanylate kinase-like (GK) domain [[cite:PUB00026723], [cite:PUB00075264]]. In the MPP proteins, this core is often preceded by one or two L27 domains that mediate homo- and heterodimerisation [[cite:PUB00035412], [cite:PUB00166510]], while in CASK and LIN-2, the core is preceded by an N-terminal calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase (CaMK) domain [[cite:PUB00128518], [cite:PUB00050845]]. The PDZ-SH3-GK tandem forms a structural supramodule that binds to the cytoplasmic tails of transmembrane proteins, such as Crumbs (Crb) and neurexins, regulating cell polarity, junctional integrity, and synaptic function [[cite:PUB00075264], [cite:PUB00166511]]. For example, PALS1 (MPP5) links the Crumbs complex to other polarity proteins [[cite:PUB00156450]], while CASK interacts with neurexins and syndecans to mediate synaptic transmembrane protein anchoring and ion channel trafficking [[cite:PUB00036131], [cite:PUB00050845]].
